cells.tense: You are standing at fair exchange and can see the whole shape of it.
cells.ask: Name one exchange you and another have already settled, in one sentence, out loud, before the day gets loud.
cells.core:
You are standing in a fair exchange where giving and receiving have come back level, and you can see the whole shape of the trade while you stand inside it. The line where one side stopped and the other began is visible to you without any effort. That cuts both ways. You can call a bad trade early, and you can leave a good one alone instead of evening it out one more time.

When the pattern is held loosely, the exchange itself is trusted. One side gives today, the other gives tomorrow, and you let that be true. The measure stays loose and the trade still works. Feed that. The task is not to hold the line tighter; it is to let one exchange stand at what it already is when it comes up next, and not one adjustment past that.

cells.verb: trading fairly through the felt exchange between people

cells.tense: You are ahead of the fairness, deciding what each side will owe before anything has actually moved.
cells.ask: Leave one exchange you have already weighed exactly where it stands, and do not add a single item to either side before it moves again.
cells.core:
You are running the math ahead of the exchange. The balance is not here yet, but you have already worked out what each side owes and what you will have to do to make it fair. So a conversation can turn into an audit, and a kindness comes pre-paid with a number on it. You are carrying the whole ledger instead of letting it pass between you.

Somewhere ahead there is a settling up that would let you rest. That settling keeps moving because the math is going on in your head, not between two people. The fair thing is usually a clear read on what is right, and it changes with the exchange in front of you. Hold one trade this week without improving it.

cells.tense: You have been silent at a door where giving and receiving once moved between you.
cells.ask: Pick one small exchange with someone you trust and take only your side of it, once, without working out what will come back.
cells.core:
You have been quiet at the place where trades happen. Giving and receiving have felt like something to keep track of, so you stopped putting much into the circle. Now you mostly give or mostly hold back, and the exchange does not really start. What is missing is not generosity; it is the ability to be part of a fair trade, even badly.

When the exchange is working, one motion carries both sides, and you can enter it without deciding the outcome first. Pick one small thing and take only your side of it. Say what you sent, without asking about the return, and let it have its own life from there.

cells.tense: You are already reading the pattern through what is given and what is returned.
cells.ask: Say out loud the one trade where your own reading was right, before you go back to keeping it to yourself.
cells.core:
You are already reading the shape of what is fair between people. You catch the small signal — a word, a moment, something two people will not say — and you know what it means about who is giving and who is taking before it is spoken. You keep it to yourself and call it just how things are, but the reading is there and it is yours.

The pattern you see is what fairness looks like from where you sit. The exchange runs on what you know, without anyone saying what they know, so the trade goes on with no one owning the truth that moved in it. The confirmation lands without argument when it is said, and saying it out loud makes it truer, not harder. Name one trade and your read of it.
